why_this_exists: The allowance lives in ONE row, ingestion_state.bettor_live_probe_state,
and `obs-arm` replaces it wholesale with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. Replacing
a row is not preserving its history: the moment the replacement probe is
armed, every trace of this one is gone from the database. This file is
the copy, written BEFORE that happened.
outcome: NEVER RAN. Refused its own first reservation and spent nothing.

defect.summary: The reserver refused every request because it was handed no pool.
detail: workers/all.py registers the loop as bettor_live_loop.main and the
supervisor calls it WITH NO ARGUMENTS, so control_pool is None.
read_control, read_budget and reserve all resolve None through
_resolve() -> get_pool(), which is why the control read true and the
allowance read open. The _reserve closure did not: it treated None as
'there is no pool' and refused everything.
second_defect_found_after: disarm took a pool directly and main() guarded both call sites with
control_pool is not None -- always false in production -- so the
deadline's automatic shutdown would have written nothing at all.
third_defect_found_after: _read_one_sync reads getattr(client, 'markets'), and main() with no
arguments passed client=None into probe(). _list_candidates resolved
its own client so the LISTING worked and hid it; every BBO read would
have returned 'client.markets.bbo is absent', spending the whole
allowance on reads that never left the process.

it_failed_closed.note: The ceilings were never at risk. The probe simply could not run.

do_not: Do not reset, replenish or extend this allowance.
A replacement probe takes a NEW probe_id after this one is closed.
